The readme says ky uppercases standard HTTP method names so servers that are case-sensitive about methods don't reject the request. That only works when the method is passed in all lowercase. If I pass a mixed-case standard method, for example `ky('https://example.com', {method: 'Patch'})`, the request goes out with the method `Patch` exactly as written, and servers reject it.

Expected: any standard method (get, post, put, patch, head, delete, options, trace, query) is sent uppercased no matter how it is cased, so `'Patch'`, `'pOsT'` and `'patch'` all go out as `PATCH`/`POST`. Custom, non-standard method names should still be sent unchanged.

The `parseJson` option is ignored when I call `.json()` on a cloned response. `(await ky.get(url, {parseJson: customParser})).json()` uses my parser, but `response.clone().json()` uses the native `JSON.parse` instead. The same thing happens when cloning the response inside an `afterResponse` hook, and when cloning the response returned while `onDownloadProgress` is set.

Expected: a clone of a ky response behaves like the original. `clone().json()` should call the custom `parseJson` with the same arguments (the text plus the same `request` and `response` context) in all of those cases. Clones of clones should work too.

With `onDownloadProgress` set, the response ky returns is missing some of the original response's metadata. `response.url` is an empty string, `response.redirected` is `false` even when the request was redirected, and `response.type` doesn't match the real response. Without `onDownloadProgress` all three are correct.

Expected: turning on `onDownloadProgress` should not change `url`, `redirected` or `type`. They should match what the underlying fetch response reports, including on a `response.clone()` of that response and on responses with no body (such as 204).
